text:
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT created — polarishealth-corp dedicated pool 'polaris-dedicated-1' GPU saturation. Severity: P1. Trigger: 95% GPU util (measured across pool), queueing seen for tenant polarishealth-corp. Pagerduty: paging on-call.

sam_h: got the page, joining. any customer-facing impact reported yet?

mika_r: metrics show all 8 gpus in the pool are at 98%. tail latency > 3s for polarishealth requests. non-polaris tenants not affected (isolation still working). looks like polaris sent sustained large batch jobs since 21:12 UTC.

alex_g: confirms. autoscaler didn't trigger because pool at max replicas (8). policy is "reserved-max=8" for this enterprise. we have burst capacity configured but needs manual approval (cost ack).

jeff_sre: tagging product + cse. lia_cse can we get customer on a quick call? want to confirm if this is expected training/ingestion job.

lia_cse: pinging Polaris on the support channel now. their support says "we kicked off a model sweep" around 20:50 and expected it to use dedicated infra, will check if they can throttle.

ops-bot: recent events: 
- 21:06 polarishealth-corp created 1200 concurrent requests
- 21:08 3 large-batch jobs spawned (batch_size=512)
- 21:14 queue depth increased x6

sam_h: mitigation options on the table:
1) enable burst override -> add 4 GPUs from pool-burst (costly, immediate)
2) temporarily route polaris requests to hosted fallback model variant (lower throughput but keeps calls alive)
3) throttle polaris batch jobs via rate-limit policy + ask customer to reduce batch sizes
4) evict noncritical background workloads from pool (not many present)

mika_r: quick checks: available burst slots = 4 (in us-west-2), time to spin = ~90s. fallback models: optimized-medium has ~200ms extra latency but available.

alex_g: recommend immediate combination: 1) enable burst override (short lived) AND 2) apply routing rule to send >batch-size=128 to fallback to reduce queue. That buys time while lia gets confirmation from customer.

jeff_sre: agree. who can authorize burst? oncall cost-approver tag required (engineering lead or product lead).

sam_h: i'm oncall lead, i can approve up to $2000 immediate spend for incidents. this looks like < $2000 for a short burst. approve it.

irene_ops: i'll execute the burst override and update autoscaler to allow temporary scale to 12. running command now:
```
opsctl burst enable --pool polaris-dedicated-1 --add-gpus 4 --reason "incident polarishealth high load"
```

irene_ops: opsctl returned: request accepted, allocating 4 GPUs from pool-burst-3. expected ready in 85s.

mika_r: applying temporary routing rule to split heavy batches:
```
routectl add-rule --pool polaris-dedicated-1 --condition "batch_size > 128 AND tenant == polarishealth-corp" --action fallback:hosted:optimized-medium --ttl 600
```

mika_r: rule applied. monitoring queues.

ops-bot: burst allocation complete. 4 GPUs added to polaris-dedicated-1. Pool now at 12 GPUs.

sam_h: signal check?

mika_r: GPU util dropped to 72% across pool; queue depth halved. tail latency trending down to ~650ms. good.

lia_cse: Polaris on support call: they confirm the sweep was accidental (dev branch script loop). they've paused the jobs and will restart with smaller batch sizes. asking for guidance on recommended batch_size <= 64 for our dedicated.

sam_h: note for post-incident: update docs and tenant onboarding guidance. but immediate: do we keep burst on for another 20m to ensure clean drain?

alex_g: yes keep for 20m, then rollback to reserved-max=8. also create an incident tag for billing and mark it as customer-approved mitigation. lia to confirm.

lia_cse: customer verbally approved temporary burst and will accept cost share. I'll get signed confirmation in the ticket.

jeff_sre: i'll prepare rollback plan and postmortem checklist:
- revoke burst after drain
- remove routing rule after 30m
- check autoscaler logs for why it hit max earlier
- suggest server-side guardrails (max concurrent for sweep jobs)

irene_ops: scheduling rollback at 21:50 UTC +30m from now. will run:
```
opsctl burst disable --pool polaris-dedicated-1 --remove-gpus 4 --reason "post-incident rollback"
```

mika_r: adding monitoring alerts to watch for any re-spike and to alert cse if polaris resumes big-batch jobs.

ops-bot: incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. next steps: lia to update customer ticket, jeff to own postmortem, sam to follow up for ops playbook changes.

sam_h: handing off to night oncall (jeff_sre) for monitoring and postmortem follow-up. I'm available if pager goes off.

jeff_sre: acknowledged, taking over. I'll keep the incident channel updated if anything changes.

lia_cse: ticket updated with customer acknowledgement and cost note. assigning billing follow-up to finance@redwood.

jeff_sre: closing notes for handoff: burst enabled at 21:18 UTC, pool scaled to 12, latency recovered by 21:22 UTC, customer paused jobs at 21:24 UTC, rollback scheduled 21:50 UTC.

pagerduty-bot: Incident resolved (mitigated). Will auto-close after 4 hours if no regressions.

sam_h: thank you team. please add any observations to the postmortem doc.

jeff_sre: will do, starting draft now.

(reacts: :thumbsup: from lia_cse, :eyes: from mika_r)
